title: SafeFlowMatcher: Safe and Fast Planning using Flow Matching with Control Barrier Functions
claim: Prior methods enforce safety on intermediate samples during generation and get distorted or trapped; ours decouples generation from certification to get a complete, safe result.
layout: 2 stacked rows split by a horizontal divider, sharing a left-hand initial noise panel; left-to-right arrows labeled Integration, prior on top and ours on bottom
description: The figure has two horizontal rows separated by a black divider. A shared starting panel on the left shows a scatter of grey-blue noise dots, a robot, an obstacle (a dark pit with a shovel and a no-entry sign), and a house as the goal. The top row, labeled 'Other certification-based Methods', has an arrow labeled '+ Certified safety Integration'. It leads to a distorted dot path with orange-circled corrections, then to a final path with red blobs and the label 'Trapped' in red. The bottom row, labeled 'SafeFlowMatcher (our)', has a 'Prediction Integration' arrow to a path that crosses the obstacle. A 'Correction + Certified safety Integration' arrow then leads to orange-highlighted dots at the obstacle and a clean path around it. Orange marks the safety steps and red marks the failure. Dots shade from light to dark along each path.
caption: Overview of SafeFlowMatcher Versus Existing Certification-Based Methods. Directly constraining intermediate samples during generation (top) can cause paths to be distorted or trapped, whereas SafeFlowMatcher (bottom) decouples generation and certification, producing a complete and certified-safe path.
abstract: Generative planners based on flow matching (FM) produce high-quality paths in a single or a few ODE steps, but their sampling dynamics offer no formal safety guarantees and can yield incomplete paths near constraints. We present SafeFlowMatcher, a planning framework that couples FM with control barrier functions (CBFs) to achieve both real-time efficiency and certified safety. SafeFlowMatcher uses a two-phase (PC) integrator: (i) a prediction phase integrates the learned FM once (or a few steps) to obtain a candidate path without intervention; (ii) a correction phase refines this path with a vanishing time-scaled vector field and a CBF-based quadratic program that minimally perturbs the vector field. We prove a barrier certificate for the resulting flow system, establishing forward invariance of a robust safe set and finite-time convergence to the safe set. In addition, by enforcing safety only on the executed path, rather than all intermediate latent paths, SafeFlowMatcher avoids distributional drift and mitigates local trap problems. Moreover, SafeFlowMatcher attains faster, smoother, and safer paths than diffusion- and FM-based baselines on maze navigation, locomotion, and robot manipulation tasks. Extensive ablations corroborate the contributions of the PC integrator and the barrier certificate.
